source_title: Three flown to Melbourne hospitals after tourist mini-van rolls on island
source_excerpt:
Ten people were travelling in the mini-van when it rolled. ( ABC News: Monte Bovill )
A group of 10 have survived with a range of injuries after their hired minibus rolled after coming off the road on King Island on Friday.
Police say the group were all visitors to King Island from the mainland, aged in their mid-70s to 80s.
Crews from Tasmania and Victoria were involved in the emergency response.
A group of 10 have survived after their hired minibus rolled after losing traction in gravel on King Island on Friday.
Tasmania Police said about 4.20pm on Friday, a Toyota HiAce passenger van, with a "group of elderly people on board was involved in a single-vehicle crash on South Road, Pearshape, in the rural south of the island".
The group were all visitors to King Island from the mainland, aged in their mid-70s to 80s.
Following the response by emergency services at the scene and at King Island Hospital, three patients were flown by Air Ambulance Victoria fixed-wing aircraft to Melbourne on Friday night.
One patient was admitted to The Alfred Hospital and remains in a stable condition. Two patients were admitted to Royal Melbourne Hospital.
Seven patients were initially admitted to King Island District Hospital and Health Centre at Currie.
Police said three of those patients have since been transferred to the Royal Hobart Hospital with minor and moderate injuries. All three patients at the Royal Hobart Hospital remain in a stable condition.
Four patients remained on King Island for treatment at the King Island District Hospital and Health Centre.
Three were medically cleared and discharged to their accommodation late last night. One patient was kept for observation overnight and has now been discharged.
Van went down embankment and rolled, police say
Police said initial investigations suggested the vehicle failed to take a bend on the road, losing traction in loose gravel.
The van went down an embankment, rolled over and landed back on its wheels.
Passengers and the driver sustained various injuries including suspected fractures, facial trauma, back pain and complaints of internal pain.
Some of the patients had serious injuries, although none were believed to be life-threatening.
Tasmania Police Inspector Steve Jones praised the crash response by emergency services, including volunteer units.
"This was quite a challenging incident involving a significant crash, multiple people with serious injuries, and in a remote location," he said.
"The crash scene was quite complex, so the quick response and the level of care and assistance that the patients received from police and those in the volunteer emergency services, until such time as the specialist medical teams arrived, was outstanding.
"A number of resources were deployed which included volunteer emergency services in Ambulance Tasmania, the State Emergency Service and Tasmania Fire Service. A further call was put out to the mine at Grassy to provide their ambulance, which they did.
"Given the number of casualties, their age and the potential severity of injuries, a fixed-wing ambulance aircraft was deployed from Victoria and both Westpac Rescue Helicopters with medical staff onboard were tasked from Hobart.
Ambulance Tasmania Chief Executive Nicole Ashworth also praised the emergency response.
"I want to thank our ambulance volunteers, paramedics, medical retrieval teams and all the emergency services who responded", she said.
"This includes our colleagues at Ambulance Victoria, for their exceptional response to yesterday's incident on King Island.
Tasmania Police investigations into the crash are continuing.
Anyone with information about the crash, dashcam footage, or who may have seen the white van travelling on South Road, Pearshape, around the time of the incident, is asked to contact Police on 131444.
'Sharp bends' for drivers, acting mayor says
Acting King Island Mayor Vernon Philbey said he was "thinking very much" of the injured people.
"It's not a good way to visit King Island … I hope they all get well," he said.
The incident happened at the beginning of a "very busy" long weekend at King Island, with an annual golf tournament drawing visitors from interstate.
"It could have been some of the golfers … we don't know," Cr Philbey said.
